ai.title: Add cloud chat rollback types and client method
ai.summary: The shared cloud history contract in common now supports rolling back a chat to a previous run. Two new types, CloudHistoryChatRollback and CloudHistoryChatRolledBack, model the request payload and the response, with the response mode distinguishing between cut, note, and unchanged agent memory states. The createCloudHistoryClient factory gains a rollbackChat method that issues a POST request to the chats/{chatId}/rollback endpoint, returning the updated chat and rollback mode. This extends the Postgres-backed cloud history API with a new chat state mutation alongside existing fork and update operations.
ai.evidence: The diff in common/src/desktop-cloud/history.ts introduces the CloudHistoryChatRollback and CloudHistoryChatRolledBack types and adds the rollbackChat method to the client factory.

facts: A compact never starts a session, so pressing it again would meet the same refusal.

Rethrow a request the API or provider refused (thrown by the stream: a session that ended, a policy refusal, a BYOK 4xx), so the run ends on that refusal as a turn's request would. An in-band failure (a 5xx or a cut stream, an empty reply) still returns null: trying again can work.
A manual compact's summary is the run's only request, so its refusal (a session that ended, a policy refusal) is the run's outcome: "try again" would only be refused again (prod 11-02..04).
What a compact did, from its callbacks: a pass that began and installed nothing failed.
The run's own signal: its abort is logged and rethrown.
entries.title: Shared/Core update: compact
entries.summary: Shared/Core, Agent Runtime changes across 3 file(s) (+89/−1).

ai.title: Manual compact rethrows API refusals and adds session-ended message
ai.summary: The agent runtime now distinguishes provider refusals from transient errors during conversation summarization. A new `rethrowRefusals` flag in `packages/agent-runtime/src/conversation-summary.ts` causes `summarizeAndLog` to rethrow errors that are not `SummaryError` or aborts, effectively propagating API or provider rejections to the caller. This flag is enabled only for manual compactions in `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts` via `rethrowRefusals: options.trigger === 'manual'`, ensuring that if a /compact request is refused because a session ended or by policy, the run ends on that refusal rather than failing silently. A new constant `CLOUD_COMPACT_SESSION_ENDED` in `common/src/desktop-cloud/compact.ts` provides a user-facing message explaining that the chat's session ended, alongside one other change.
ai.evidence: The `summarizeAndLog` function in `packages/agent-runtime/src/conversation-summary.ts` adds a `rethrowRefusals` parameter and corresponding catch block logic; `loopAgentSteps` in `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts` passes `rethrowRefusals: options.trigger === 'manual'` to it; `common/src/desktop-cloud/compact.ts` exports `CLOUD_COMPACT_SESSION_ENDED`.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show how the rethrown refusal is handled by the CLI or SDK layers that consume the run's output.

changes.what: Added `rethrowRefusals` parameter to `summarizeAndLog` and wired it for manual compactions in `loopAgentSteps`.
Exported `CLOUD_COMPACT_SESSION_ENDED` constant for session-ended messaging in compact flows.
Updated tests in `compact-context-loop.test.ts` to verify that manual summary refusals end the run with status and code.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to clean up a long chat, it can now tell you clearly if your chat session has ended instead of staying silent. This helps you know when to start a new chat before trying to clean up the history. You will see a specific message explaining that your session has ended and how to start a new one.

entries.title: Shared/Core update: apply-patch

ai.title: Repair invented tool names and invalid JSON escapes
ai.summary: The SDK now resolves invented tool names via `TOOL_NAME_ALIASES`, and argument JSON with invalid backslash escapes, raw control characters, or unclosed arrays via new repairs in `common/src/tools/repair-tool-json.ts`. In the agent runtime, `repairCustomToolInput` replaces the previous string-encoded union repair, clamping numbers above a schema `maximum` and decoding JSON-encoded strings for parameters expecting objects or arrays. These fixes target common model slips observed in Solar Pro 4 and Flash, and DeepSeek V4 Flash traces.
ai.evidence: The diff adds `TOOL_NAME_ALIASES` and `escapeLoneBackslashes` to `common/src/tools/repair-tool-json.ts`, and replaces `repairStringEncodedUnionMembers` with `repairCustomToolInput` in `packages/agent-runtime` to clamp numeric inputs and decode JSON-encoded strings using `parseToolJson`.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not specify the rollout schedule or which model versions first exhibit these exact failures beyond the cited November 2026 traces.

changes.what: Extended tool JSON repair capabilities with new backslash escape fixes and tool name alias resolution.
Replaced string-encoded union repair with a generalized custom tool input repair that clamps values and decodes structured strings.
Integrated tool name alias resolution and JSON repair into the AI SDK stream processing for graceful error handling.

eli5.text: The assistant now recognizes made-up tool names and automatically replaces them with the correct built-in commands, so it can execute your requests without failing. It also fixes minor formatting mistakes, such as unescaped backslashes or missing brackets, in the instructions it sends to the AI, ensuring these commands are understood correctly. This improves the reliability of the assistant for anyone using the free tier, reducing instances where a task stops because the AI misunderstood its own available tools.

ai.title: Sites guidance adds option to suppress cloud browser test limits
ai.summary: The `sitesGuidance` function in `common/src/sites/guidance.ts` now accepts an optional `cloudBrowserAvailable` flag to control when a specific limitation note is appended to cloud-mode prompts. Previously, the note stating that cloud environments lack browser automation tools was always included for cloud runtimes; it is now conditionally omitted when browser availability is indicated. This change allows the shared standing guidance to adapt its verification instructions based on the actual tooling capabilities of the target harness without altering desktop behavior.
ai.evidence: In `common/src/sites/guidance.ts`, the `sitesGuidance` function signature adds a third options: { cloudBrowserAvailable?: boolean } = {} parameter, and the trailing template literal condition changes from runtime === 'cloud' to runtime === 'cloud' && !options.cloudBrowserAvailable before emitting the browser-test limitation note.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show which caller sets the new option or how the browser availability state is determined.

eli5.text: The standing instructions for the cloud-based web hosting feature now include a new option to skip a specific warning about the lack of browser automation tools. This warning is now only shown when the system confirms that browser tools are actually unavailable in the cloud environment. This is an internal update to the guidance system that allows the assistant to adapt its verification steps to the specific capabilities of the current workspace, and it does not change how desktop users interact with the service.
